title: An Elegy for the Landline
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] We disconnected the landline last week, a decision so trivially administrative that I'm faintly embarrassed by how long I mourned it afterward.
Narrator: Nobody had dialed that number in years except telemarketers and, twice annually, an aunt who distrusts anything with a screen attached to it.

Narrator: [carefully] And yet there was a particular anguish, unearned and entirely disproportionate, to watching the technician disconnect a cord that had, decades ago, delivered every significant piece of news my family ever received.
Narrator: I keep catching myself romanticizing an object I hadn't consciously thought about in a decade, which tells you less about the telephone than about how selectively nostalgia operates.

Narrator: [reflective] It wasn't the ringing I missed, precisely, but the specific vulnerability the ringing implied: you answered without knowing who waited on the other end, an intimacy the caller identification on my phone has quietly, efficiently abolished.
Narrator: Every call now arrives pre-vetted, filtered through a name and a photograph, stripped of the small, bracing uncertainty that used to precede even the most mundane conversation.

Narrator: [honestly] I suspect what I'm actually grieving isn't the hardware at all but a mode of attention the hardware once enforced: a call demanded your whole, undivided presence, since nothing else was competing for it in that moment.
Narrator: My smartphone offers infinitely more, and asks correspondingly less of me, which is either an extraordinary bargain or a slow, imperceptible theft, and I genuinely cannot decide which.
Narrator: [gently] I'm not proposing we resurrect the landline; that would be sentimentality masquerading as principle, and I have little patience for either in myself.

Narrator: But I have started, deliberately, answering calls without first consulting the screen, reintroducing a sliver of that old, bracing uncertainty into a life that has otherwise been thoroughly, comfortably pre-vetted.
